title: Signal scrapbook — raw asks and quick fixes
content:
Purpose:
- Scratchpad for frontline snippets and tiny actionables from CS, pre-triage. Use to feed sprint micro-tasks and 'fix-in-a-day' ideas. Not polished; mostly verbatim customer lines + quick proposals.

Topline signal clusters (raw counts from Feb 1–14 inbound threads):
- Request: per-route token-cost breakdown (14) — customers want embedded-level granularity by model/route. Comments: 'We need to know which route is burning tokens so we can nudge payback metrics.'
- Request: more tolerant fallback behavior for short bursts (9) — apps see spikes; want soft-fallback that preserves output shape.
- Request: shorter cold-start on Dedicated (7) — customers with reservation see first-call latency spikes.
- Request: CLI-friendly private deploy artifacts (6) — engineers want tarball + config example for air-gapped installs.
- Ask: official guidance for quantized model quality checks (5) — 'how to know if 4-bit will break my prompts?'

Representative raw quotes (verbatim-ish):
- 'Our billing dashboard is a black box when we use multi-route flows.' — mid-market fintech
- 'Can you make the fallback more like a graceful degradation and not a 500? We lose users.' — consumer app
- 'We have a dedicated cluster but the first 3 requests after idle are 2.5s — unacceptable for our UX.' — SaaS search vendor
- 'Give us a single-file private deploy we can hand to infra in an offline environment.' — regulated healthcare customer

Quick-fixes (<= 2 dev-days) — hypotheses and owners:
- Add per-route token estimate column to Billing UI (mock up + backend tag). Owner: Priya P. Effort: 1.5d. Risk: low (read-only). Impact: high for cost-sensitive customers.
- Fallback wrapper: change 500->200 with 'degraded' envelope on short capacity misses (API-level). Owner: Marcus L. Effort: 2d (api + docs). Risk: medium (client parsing).
- Dedicated warm-call shim: client-side small warm-up helper snippet (node/python) + doc. Owner: Diego. Effort: 1d. Impact: immediate UX improvement for some customers.

Longer/roadmap asks (need product + eng triage)
- Per-route SLOs + automatic fallback routing: customers want policy-level controls that route by cost vs latency. Suggested PRD: outline routing policies, UI rule builder, and evaluation matrix. Approx effort: 6–8 sprints cross-team. Linked: CS-3421.
- Private deploy single-archive installer: productize the airgap bundle with KMS handshake examples. Needs legal & security review.
- Quantization QC guide + eval harness: produce a checklist + example prompts; tie to Optimize recommendations.

Customer-impact heatmap (qualitative):
- High impact, easy fix: Billing UI per-route (14 requests)
- High impact, medium effort: graceful fallback (9 requests; affects production reliability)
- Medium impact, short-term: dedicated warm-call shim (7 requests)
- Lower frequency but strategic: private deploy artifacts & quantization docs

Open questions / unknowns:
- For per-route billing: do we have model->route attribution in logs today? If not, what's the gap? (Asked to infra on Feb 20)
- Fallback change: what client SDKs parse errors today? Need matrix (JS/Python/Go).
- Dedicated cold-start: are spikes caused by autoscaler spin-up or model kernel load? SRE to validate with trace data.

Suggested next steps (short):
1) Priya: mock Billing UI column + screenshot by 2024-02-21. Attach to billing-sprint ticket.
2) Marcus: prototype API envelope for degraded responses, demo to CS by 2024-02-23.
3) Diego: publish warm-call shim snippet to snippets repo and add to onboarding doc by 2024-02-22.
4) CS: compile top 5 customers who reported each issue (owner: Ava) and attach to JIRA tickets for prioritization.

Known ask mapping (initial ticket seeds):
- Per-route billing -> JIRA: CS-3509 (seeded)
- Graceful fallback -> JIRA: CS-3510 (seeded)
- Dedicated warm-call shim -> internal-snippets#warm-call-1

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Might be able to reuse retired telemetry tag 'route.id' instead of adding new logging. Check with infra tagging.
- PRD for routing policies should include 'cost cap' condition (e.g., if estimated cost > X then route to cheaper variant).
- Consider a short live webinar for top affected customers explaining warm-call shim + fallback behavior.

Appendix: raw thread ids / quick refs (for digging)
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03ABCXY/p1676500000000000
- Top complainant email: acct-472@customer.com (internal ticket link attached)
- Confluence capture: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CS-feedback-2024Q1

This doc is intentionally messy. Use as source for sprint micro-tasks. If something moves to a ticket, please update that ticket and delete the line in this doc or mark it resolved.

-- Diego M. (CS)
